name: Why do caulk lines and trim paint crack in Denver-area homes?

mainEntity.name: Why do caulk lines and trim paint crack in Denver-area homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homes along the Front Range experience low ambient humidity and significant seasonal temperature swings that cause interior wood framing and trim to expand and contract. This movement regularly pulls caulk lines open where baseboards meet drywall and opens mitered casing corners. For homes in Denver, Aurora, Centennial, and Parker, trim painting requires high-flexibility elastomeric caulking that stretches without splitting during dry winter months, alongside thorough sanding to ensure acrylic enamels adhere cleanly through shifting indoor conditions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Colorado's dry climate and seasonal temperature shifts cause framing lumber to expand and contract. Flexible elastomeric caulk is essential to keep trim joints from cracking open.
